lines.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Heritage Field! Today, the Richmond Falcons visit your Madison Kings.
Now batting, number 23, Tyler Vance.
Now pitching, number 41, Leo Brooks.
Fireworks after the game tonight, weather permitting.
Strike three!
Ball four!
Play ball!
Safe!
Foul ball!
Fouled back, four-seam fastball, off the plate.
Swung on and missed, cutter, 88.
Curveball, 78, down and in.
The three and oh pitch... slider, high.
Riley Perez grounds out, 5-3.
Mario Sanders lays down a sacrifice bunt, 5-4-3.
After four, it's Eugene Giants 4, Albany Owls 3.
Fly ball to left field, he drifts back, back, to the track, and he makes the catch at the wall.
The Falcons: 55 and 53 on the year, seven and three over their last ten.
Good afternoon, everybody, and welcome to Heritage Field, where the Kings host the Richmond Falcons on a Tuesday afternoon in late July. Lyle Pemberton here, next to Hollis Dupree.
Deep drive to left... gone! Home run!
Gone! And the game is over, a walk-off homer!
Pack a lunch, that one is going a long way!
Two for one. Everything must go!
Sit down, son.
Put this one in the books.
Hot. Somebody bring the catchers a towel.
Mm-hmm. Biscuits and gravy.
That is a grown-man swing.
I would not have thrown him out either. Ask any pitcher I ever caught.
He sits around 91 with the fastball. The curveball is his best pitch, a 65 on the scouting scale, and he throws it every so often.
Biscuit to everybody but my mother, Lyle. Good to be here.
We have a question from a young fan, Biscuit: why do they call you Biscuit?
Double-A, a Sunday doubleheader, and a basket of buttermilk biscuits. I ate eleven between games, Lyle. Went oh for eight.
Oh for eight. And they still remember the biscuits.
Number six was a grand slam, Lyle. In my defense, the wind was blowing out.
The wind was blowing out. Of course it was.

pbp.text: Twenty-six seasons in this booth, and I still keep the scorebook in pencil. Here is the next pitch, and it is fouled back out of play.

color.text: I caught for eleven seasons, and I can tell you, he is setting him up for the curveball. Watch where the catcher sets up his glove.

pa.text: Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, welcome to the ballpark. Please rise and remove your caps for our national anthem.

ump.text: Strike! That is ball two. Batter, take your base. Play ball! He is out!

calibration: Welcome back to the ballpark. Here is the pitch, and it is a called strike on the outside corner. The count runs to one and one.
